name: Ambalappuzha Sree Krishna Temple
tagline: Historic Parthasarathy shrine famed for Ambalappuzha palpayasam and ritual–astrology links
summary: 15th–17th century Parthasarathy Krishna temple in Ambalappuzha, famous for the daily Ambalappuzha palpayasam. Ritual timing and festival dates follow the Malayalam lunar/nakshatra calendar and…
description: Ambalappuzha Sree Krishna Temple is a historic Vaishnava shrine in Alappuzha district where Lord Krishna is worshipped in the Parthasarathy form. The present temple complex reflects traditional Kerala temple architecture and mural work and dates in local accounts to the 15th–17th centuries.

The temple is best known across Kerala for its daily Ambalappuzha palpayasam — a simple, slowly cooked milk-and-rice prasadam that is offered to the deity before distribution. The palpayasam tradition and the chessboard legend behind it form a central part of the temple’s identity.

Temple ritual timing and major events follow the Malayalam lunar and nakshatra calendar (for example the installation/Arattu observance links to Moolam day). That calendaric scheduling connects the temple’s festival sequence and midday offerings with local jyotisha (astrological) practice and remedial vows (vazhipadu) taken by devotees.

Today the shrine is administered under the Travancore Devaswom Board. Visitors come for darshan, to receive palpayasam, and to arrange time-sensitive offerings or homams — especially around festival days when bookings and collection windows are strict. Confirm details with the temple office before you travel.
highlights: Daily Ambalappuzha palpayasam — famous milk-and-rice prasadam
Krishna as Parthasarathy (charioteer form) and rich mural panels
Festival calendar tied to Malayalam nakshatra days (e.g., Moolam)
Active site for time‑sensitive vows, offerings and remedial rites
Managed by Travancore Devaswom Board; nearby Ambalappuzha railway station

sections.heading: Background
body: Local histories place the shrine’s building and prominence between the 15th and 17th centuries under the Chembakassery line; the temple later becomes one of Kerala’s important Vaishnava centres. The layout follows Kerala temple architecture with a nalambalam, chuttambalam and a temple tank.
A well known legend links the palpayasam offering to a royal debt and a chess game; the story explains why the temple continues the uninterrupted tradition of serving palpayasam to devotees.

sections.heading: Rituals and astrology (jyotisha) connections
body: Temple rituals and festival dates follow the Malayalam lunar calendar and nakshatra (star) observances. The shrine’s annual and special observances are scheduled around specific nakshatra days — for example the installation/Arattu ceremonies associate with Moolam day, which also ties into the nearby Champakulam Moolam boat race.

Local jyotisha practitioners and temple priests commonly coordinate on timing for vows (vazhipadu), homams and remedial rites; devotees who consult an astrologer often schedule offerings and remedial ceremonies to match muhurta (auspicious times) recommended by the astrologer. If you plan remedial rites tied to personal astrology, confirm muhurta, booking and required materials with the temple office in advance.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Attend morning or evening puja and view the Parthasarathy murti and painted panels inside the nalambalam. The simple, slow-cooked palpayasam offered at midday is the temple’s signature experience — receiving it as prasadam is part of the pilgrimage for many visitors.

If your interest is ritual-astrology, ask the temple office about available homams, yajnas or vow‑offerings and whether specific muhurta slots are available. Time your visit to festival days if you want to see traditional performances such as Ottanthullal and the Arattu procession during main festivals.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Typical visitor hours are approximately 04:00–12:30 and 17:00–20:00 but festival or special puja days change this schedule; palpayasam distribution aligns with the midday offering, so plan around that window. The nearest railhead is Ambalappuzha Railway Station (about 1–1.5 km).

For palpayasam and time-sensitive offerings: check availability and book in advance when possible, verify the current price and collection window, and call the Devaswom office if the online booking does not list palpayasam for your date. Confirm dress code, photography rules and any local instructions before you attend.

latest.text: Detailed visitor guide and official-style update reports a revised palpayasam rate and booking details for 2026; advises that palpayasam collection is tied to the midday offering and to confirm availability before travel.
New Indian Express publishes a detailed piece on the palpayasam legend and preparation, listing quantities and the traditional preparation schedule used at the temple.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Visit in the dry months (October–March) for comfortable weather; plan festival visits by Malayalam calendar (Moolam day and local festival dates).
visitorInfo.howToReach: By train: Ambalappuzha Railway Station (~1–1.5 km). By road: 14 km south of Alappuzha town on SH‑12. Nearest airport: Cochin International Airport (COK).
etiquette: If palpayasam is essential to your visit, book or confirm it in advance — collection is tied to the midday offering and quantities run out on festival days.
Dress modestly and follow the temple’s dress code; leave footwear and bags in the designated area. Confirm photography rules at the counter.
For remedial rites or homams arranged on astrological advice, bring the astrologer’s muhurta details and check availability with the temple office well before the date.
Call the temple office to confirm timings, palpayasam availability and any festival closures before you travel.
